findings.title: Double-backtick escapes meant to show a literal backtick render as broken KaTeX math in the built site
locations: docs/build/architecture.html — rendered as $```math$, two instances of $$ `` (empty math plus a stray literal double backtick), and $`[^`]*[≤≥≠∈∉∇Δ⟨⟩‖√×⋅][^`]*`$
findings.description: RULE.TEX.RENDERED_MATH makes a double-backtick span this Documenter build's inline-math syntax, so wherever prose tries to use the classic Markdown double-backtick escape to display a literal backtick, a backtick-delimited regex, or the project's own `` `` ``/```math``` fence syntax as a code example, the build instead feeds that text to KaTeX as a formula. A backtick is not valid LaTeX, so the built HTML carries the raw, unrendered source ($`n`$, $```math$, bare $$ with a stray `` left over, or the full regex wrapped in $…$) instead of the intended code text — visible only by reading the built pages, never from the source alone. All 5 source lines across 2 files produce the defect; 3 of the 5 are, ironically, ARCHITECTURE.md's own worked examples of the math-notation rule they sit inside.
findings.resolution_hint: Replace each double-backtick escape with a single-backtick code span (Markdown already lets a single backtick contain a backtick by using a longer, mismatched delimiter is unnecessary here — just drop to one backtick, e.g. `` `n` `` → `` `\`n\`` `` is not needed; simplest fix is to describe the syntax in words or use a fenced fixed-width code block instead of an inline double-backtick span) so the content is never handed to KaTeX; re-run the docs build and re-grep the built HTML for `<span>$` containing a backtick to confirm the class is gone.

findings.title: Four live CLI verbs (bump, fleet, release, selftest) have no documentation anywhere on the built site
locations: docs/build/guide/verbs.html — opens "the table is closed, and every verb below is rendered from its own docstring" yet lists none of these four
docs/src/guide/verbs.md and docs/src/api/CLI.md — neither `@docs` block names Bump, Fleet, Release or Selftest

docs/build/architecture.html — the only site-wide mention of these files is as bare filenames in the §3 repository-layout listing ("Doctor.jl Sync.jl Init.jl Fleet.jl Bump.jl Release.jl Install.jl"), not a documented verb
findings.description: All four functions are real, currently-registered entries of the closed `VERBS` table and each already carries a full docstring in source, but no `@docs` block on any built page collects `bump`, `fleet`, `release` or `selftest` — the gap is visible only by cross-checking the built site's actual page-by-page coverage against the live verb registry, not from reading any single source file. guide/verbs.html's own opening sentence claims the page is the closed, drift-proof table of every verb, which is exactly the CURRENT & COMPLETE claim this omission falsifies: a reader following only the built docs cannot discover `gbg bump`, `gbg fleet`, `gbg release` or `gbg selftest` exist.
findings.resolution_hint: Add `GBGCodingTools.bump`, `GBGCodingTools.Fleet` (and its `fleet` function), `GBGCodingTools.release` and `GBGCodingTools.selftest` to an appropriate `@docs` block in docs/src/guide/verbs.md (or api/CLI.md), matching the existing per-section grouping, then rebuild and confirm all four bindings now appear under docs/build.
